high_risk_reasons.graphify/build.py: Core-path module (graphify/build.py); structural or invariant changes here can affect downstream graph/build consumers.

logic_changes: Added a _RELATION_PRIORITY table to determine the priority of edge relations during undirected graph collapse.
Updated the logic in `build_from_json` to use `_RELATION_PRIORITY` for determining which edge relation survives when two edges with different relations land on the same (src, tgt) pair.
behavior_changes: Calls now survive over references during undirected graph collapse, regardless of input order.

The deterministic sort by (source, target, relation) is no longer sufficient to resolve conflicts between different edge relations; instead, the higher-priority relation as defined in _RELATION_PRIORITY wins.
architectural_changes: Updated the relation-precedence policy to use a single edge invariant where the highest-priority relation survives during undirected graph collapse.
The `_RELATION_PRIORITY` table must be consulted for determining which of two conflicting edges should survive.
Relation precedence policy during undirected edge collapse
Preserves single-edge undirected graph invariant (no MultiGraph)
design_assumptions: Higher _RELATION_PRIORITY wins on same undirected node pair
One edge per undirected pair remains the storage model
downstream_impacts: Call graph accuracy for same node pairs
Dependency / reference graphs that rely on relation labels
Graph export and downstream static analysis consumers
behavioral_invariants: Collapse outcome stable across input order for calls vs references
